libs.note: BH-8281. The CPU caps bl_apply puts on a build session (bin/run-build.sh) and a fix round (bin/fix-round-claim.sh) on the box that runs it, so sshd, cron lanes and the pool ticks keep a reserve. Resolved through lib_env_apply build-limits <project> in a subshell, so a row lib.build-limits.<project>.<knob> sets one project tighter. Then from this file's own default in the checkout.

knobs.zero_means: auto: half the cores, at least 1
knobs.note: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS exported for the session, unless CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is already set. Only cargo reads it. On 2026-10-24 a project-6-desktop cargo build on box-project-6-os-1 took the box to load 92 and the hub could not ssh to it for 7 hours.
The niceness the build shell is reniced to (never lowered back). Its children inherit it, so a build only yields CPU under contention.
